subject: Every string the mixer.channel_strips surface exposes to AX in en-US
question: What labels does Logic show on mixer.channel_strips in en-US, and on which elements?

reverify.expected: a census in en-US whose mixer.channel_strips rows carry the same 111 distinct strings; a differing set means Logic's labels moved and every provenance citing this record wants re-reading
reverify.cost: ~1 min with Logic open on the fixture project in that locale

method: Read, never actuated. The menu bar and every menu were walked without opening them; the main window was walked to depth 8. Each element with any string became one row of the evidence file; rows were assigned to this surface by what their path or help text passes through, and rows no rule could place are counted in limits rather than filed.

strings: Audio Effect slot. Insert an audio effect. Click an occupied slot to open the plug-in. Use effects to alter signals in real time.
Bounce button. Render the signal of one or more output channel strips to an audio file, or to multiple audio files.
Channel Mode button. Click to switch the channel strip input format between Mono and Stereo. Long-click, then choose Mono, Stereo, Left, Right, or Surround from the pop-up menu.
Dim button. Set the volume according to the Dim value set in Audio General settings. Otherwise, the volume follows the master Volume fader.

EQ display. Click to add a Channel EQ or open an inserted Channel or Linear Phase EQ. Shift-click to add a Linear Phase EQ. Use EQ to shape an audio signal by adjusting the levels of specific frequency ranges.
Gain reduction meter. Shows the gain reduction of the first Compressor plug-in. If no Compressor is inserted, it shows the gain reduction of an inserted Limiter or Adaptive Limiter plug-in.
Group slot. Add the channel strip to a group. You can also define which channel strip controls can be edited for the entire group at the same time.
Input Monitoring button. Hear incoming signals on audio or software instrument tracks that aren’t record enabled. This is useful when setting levels or practicing parts before recording.

Input slot. Choose the channel strip input source. This can be an input of your audio device (your microphone or instrument is connected to) or an internal bus (to receive a signal from another channel strip).
Left inspector channel strip. Control the signal of the selected track without having to open the Mixer.
Library Focus triangle. Click to view Library content for the highlighted slot. You can also use it to open or close the Library.
MIDI Effect slot. Insert a MIDI effect. Click an occupied slot to open the plug-in.
Mastering Assistant. Click to insert Mastering Assistant.
Mute button. Silence a channel strip so it’s no longer audible. Use on an aux or output channel strip to silence that part of the mix, or on the master channel strip to mute the project.
Name field. Double-click to rename the channel strip.
Off, Sends on Faders pop-up menu. Assigns the Pan knob and Fader on channel strips to control the panning and volume of the chosen send.
Output Channel Mode button. Switches a pair of linked outputs between one stereo channel strip and two mono channel strips.
Output slot. Click and hold to choose the channel strip output destination—where the channel strip signal is sent.
Pan/Balance knob. Drag vertically to position the channel strip signal in the stereo field.
Peak Level display. Shows the signal peak during playback. Values above 0 dB turn red to indicate signal clipping. Orange values above 0 dB do not clip due to internal floating point calculations.
Record Enable button. Prepare the track for recording, or deactivate a record-ready track. The button changes to indicate whether the track is inactive, record enabled, or currently recording.

Right inspector channel strip. Shows the output channel strip for the left inspector channel strip. Shift-click the Send slot on the left inspector channel strip to show the Send Return here, or Shift-click a VCA slot in the left inspector channel strip to show the VCA channel strip here.
Send slot. Route the signal to an aux channel strip. Use sends to process or submix multiple track output signals.
Sends on Faders - On/Off. Swaps the Pan knob and Fader on channel strips so that they control the panning and volume of the chosen send.
Setting button. Load and save channel strip settings, which contain setup information for a channel strip, including plug-ins.
Show Signal Flow of Attentioned Track
Show all Channel Strips used by Tracks
Solo button. Isolate a channel strip’s signal so that it can be heard alone. Use on an aux or output channel strip to isolate that part of the mix.
Track stack disclosure arrow. Show or hide subtracks. Make sure that View > Follow Track Stacks is chosen from the Mixer menu bar.

Volume display. Shows the position of the Volume fader referenced to the dB scale to the left of the Mixer. Positive values increase the signal level, negative values decrease it, and 0 dB leaves it unchanged.

Volume fader. Set a track’s playback volume. Use on an aux or output channel strip to adjust the volume of that part of the mix. You can leave the Volume fader of the master channel strip at 0 dB in most cases.

conclusion: On this host in en-US, mixer.channel_strips exposes 212 elements carrying 111 distinct strings. Every string is in the evidence file verbatim, which is what lets a label variant cite this record: the guard requires the string to occur in the observations or evidence, and here it does or it does not.
limits: Navigation-free surfaces only: nothing behind a menu press or a button was opened, so this says nothing about the mixer, plug-in editors or the editors.
134 window rows matched no surface rule and are not filed under any record; they are in the evidence file and can be re-classified when a rule exists.
One project, one host, one build. A label that depends on project content — a track name, a region name — is a reading of this fixture, not of Logic.
